title: Customer saga: synthetic docket and feature catalysts (field notes)
summary: High-level stitched synthesis of recent customer threads (May-Jun 2028) gathered from support tickets, AE check-ins, and product trials. Focus: operational pain around multi-tenant routing, unexpected latency spikes with cached workloads, and asks for finer-grained cost controls tied to model variants. This doc converts raw signals into a compact set of feature catalysts and low-risk probes.
methodology: Pulled 87 tickets and 12 recorded calls -> quick affinity sort -> frequency banding (high/medium/low) -> cost/latency impact scoring by CS + infra heuristics -> draft probe suggestions. Prioritization bias towards items that unblock revenue (Dedicated conversions) or materially reduce per-token cost for heavy embedding customers.
clusters: Routing mismatch: customers running hybrid workloads report inconsistent routing decisions when models have near-identical performance profiles. Leads to region fallbacks and billing surprises.
KV/prefix cache invalidations: several customers observed cache churn when using streaming + tool-calls; visible as repeated early-token cost increases.
Quantization/quality regression concerns: enterprise customers hesitant to accept aggressive quantization profiles because evals are opaque and rollback tooling is limited.
Billing granularity: customers want a per-route breakdown by model variant, cache hit ratio, and batched vs non-batched token counts for chargebacks.
SLA/observability gaps: ops teams request quicker tracing hooks for requests that hit fallback policies (region/model).
feature_requests: Routing policies UI: expose an editable priority list where customers can set deterministic rules (prefer region A, prefer cheaper variant unless latency>200ms). Minimal MVP: weight + pin rules in Console.
Cache debug toggle: per-deployment toggle that logs prefix/KV cache hits and evictions (retained for 48 hours) with sample keys to help reproduce churn.
Variant billing breakdown: per-route billing export (CSV) that tags token counts by model variant, quantization level, and batch type.
Quantization trial mode: allow customers to opt into a canary that routes X% of traffic to quantized variant and surfaces a small set of hallucination/quality metrics against baseline.
Fallback trace builder: small SDK hook that captures decision path when a request falls back (region/model) and emits a one-line diagnostic included in logs and support UI.
Streaming-tool-call snapshot: record the first 3s of streaming outputs and tool-call metadata for failed sessions to aid reproductions.
Cost-saver preset templates: Console presets for 'latency-first', 'cost-first', and 'balanced' that set batching, cache TTL, quantization preference, and routing weights for quick onboarding.
impact_estimates: Routing policies UI: medium dev (4w), high business impact (reduces churn for multi-region customers; could accelerate Dedicated deals).
Cache debug toggle: low dev (2w), medium impact (fast root-cause on repeated customer tickets; reduces SRE time cost).
Variant billing breakdown: medium dev (3-5w), high impact for finance/enterprise chargeback accuracy.
Quantization trial mode: higher dev (6-8w) due to eval infra; very high impact if it unlocks quantization adoption and cost wins.
Fallback trace builder: low-med dev (3w), medium impact for support TTR (time-to-resolution).
Streaming snapshot: med dev (3-4w), helpful for diagnosing tool-call regressions and reducing customer repro requests.
Cost-saver presets: low dev (2-3w), quick UX win for PLG cohort onboarding.
sample_customer_quotes: "We see requests routed to us-east-1 even though eu-west is 20% cheaper for this model — our invoices spiked and our SREs were confused." — mid-market fintech
"When the cache churns during heavy streaming, our per-token costs jump for seemingly identical prompts. We need a way to see why keys are evicted." — AI platform team
"We like the idea of quantization but can’t risk silent quality drop. A small canary and clear metrics would help us sign up." — healthcare startup
"Give us a CSV we can drop into our chargeback pipeline that shows which model actually served each token. Current export is too aggregated." — internal platform team at large SaaS customer
open_questions: How much engineering capacity can we allocate to eval infra before delaying other roadmap items? (ask research + infra leads)
For routing policies UI, do we allow per-route overrides only in Console or expose API-first controls for IaC teams? (product decision)
What metrics are minimally sufficient for a quantization canary to be trustworthy for customers? (ops + applied-ml)
Privacy/regulatory implications of storing streaming snapshots for failed sessions (retention, PII scrub).
